applied.summary: Contradicted DF1.4 on the migration mechanism. DF1.4 declares MIGRATIONS as a flat `[table, column, decl][]` tuple list and INV-5 as 'additive only — ADD COLUMN and nothing else'; DF1.8 claimed the unique index was 'the one statement kind beyond ADD COLUMN that DF1.4's INV-5 admits'. False on both counts — the tuple shape has no slot for arbitrary DDL. Three ADD COLUMN entries stay in MIGRATIONS; `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_repo_request` moves to DF1.4's schema-init step beside its CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS DDL, and the story now records an explicit named amendment to INV-5 rather than reading permission into existing wording. `src/phase-engine/trace/schema.ts` added to Files to Modify; DoD impl line updated.

migration-invariants checklist: neither re-apply idempotency nor the rollback path was answerable from the spec alone. Now stated — re-apply is a no-op via DF1.4's `PRAGMA table_info` presence check, the list is forward-only by DF1.4's design (no down-migration), and rollback is leaving three unused nullable columns, so nothing is destructive or rewrites data. DoD adds the no-op re-apply assertion.

INV-RUN-1's NULL hole was implicit. The story used SQLite's NULL-distinct semantics to justify backward compatibility without noting the same property voids the uniqueness guard for any future session row lacking repo_slug. INV-RUN-1 now states the index binds exactly the rows carrying repo_slug (every dispatch, since AC2 rejects one without it) and that a bare DF1.4 run with no issue is outside the guarantee by construction — it mints no key and no reader here returns it.
Spec Reference clause list omitted `:36-39` (resolved-requestId rule) and `:58` (exitCode requiredness) though both are carried and cited inline in Technical Notes. Added.

The idempotency key silently under-recorded spend. `UNIQUE (run_id, agent_id, kind)` + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING cannot distinguish a redelivered event from a second genuine invocation of the same agent — DF2.7's Observability Contract states one `cost` event per pi subprocess invocation, not per run — so the second, larger invocation would be dropped, and unrecorded spend is an unenforceable cap (the story's own INV-COST-6). Re-keyed to a deterministic content digest as the `event_id` PK (over run_id, agent_id, kind, turn_count, cost_micro_usd, timestamp): a redelivered line digests identically, a genuine second invocation does not. The old key is now named as a negative control. AC1, Overview row grain, DoD impl line and DoD unit test all updated.

`request_id` was mandated NOT NULL on every ledger row with no supplier among the declared predecessors, and the Observability Contract attributed it to 'DF1.8's resolved value' — an undeclared dependency whose addition would contradict R5 §2 (DF2.8 depends on DF2.7, DF2.3, P1.2). DF2.7 explicitly scopes requestId out of CostEvent ('belongs to the DF1.4 trace store and is not introduced here') and DF2.1's twelve-field closed run record has no such field. Re-sourced to the caller at ingest and gate evaluation per DF2.1's own convention (dispatcher's id under DF3.1, CLI's minted id otherwise); an ingest invoked without one is a structured error, never a NULL row. Dependency edges left untouched and still match R5 §2.

`box_hours` rows had no possible value for the NOT NULL `role`/`agent_id` columns — a box-hour is a per-run cost with no agent, and `role` is a closed enum of agent roles. Those two columns are now nullable for that kind only, and the per-role split reports box-hours as an explicit unattributed line rather than inventing a role to satisfy a constraint.
Overview still described the row grain as one row per `(runId, agentId, kind)` after the key change; corrected to one row per emitted event.

surviving.summary: `qds cost <owner/repo>#<N>` is specified by field list (total, per-role split, per-run breakdown, cache tokens, unpriced count) with no rendering or exit-code contract beyond AC5's exit 0 on the empty case. A dev could satisfy every AC with output no test pins.

The deterministic event_id digest includes `timestamp`, which assumes DF2.7's cost event carries a redelivery-stable timestamp. DF2.7's Observability Contract does list `timestamp` on the event so the assumption holds, but its stability under redelivery is only exercised transitively by the 'replaying all three adds zero rows' test rather than asserted as a property.

`readRunPhases` appears in the Trigger Surface but only `readRunsByIssue` has a DoD contract line. AC1 requires the run be returned 'with each phase and its persisted output', so the behavior is covered; the second entry point is not separately contracted.
AC4's host-side dispatch log is located only as 'local filesystem inside the repo data boundary, mode 0600' — no concrete path, unlike the trace store's `<data_dir>/trace.db`.

`boxHourRateMicroUsd` has no default value stated. Arguably correct as-is: R5 §6 fact 11 marks exe.dev pricing vendor-single-origin [VERIFY], and the story deliberately makes the rate configuration and never a compiled constant.
